# Adjudication Task — Chapter 825

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃825화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|텔레포트 마법과 함께 터져 나온 아득한 섬광.
  6|
  7|그것이 시작이었다.
  8|
  9|주위의 공간이 일그러진다. 지금껏 느껴본 적 없는 끔찍한 압박감이 심장을 움켜쥐고, 제3의 허공으로 빨려 들어간 관절과 근육이 비명을 내지른다.
 10|
 11|‘흡.’
 12|
 13|숨이 막혔다. 고통스러웠다.
 14|
 15|불과 몇 초도 되지 않는 짧은 시간이 마치 며칠이라도 된 것처럼 길게 느껴졌다.
 16|
 17|하지만 나는 끊어지려는 의식의 끈을 붙잡고 매달렸다.
 18|
 19|까득.
 20|
 21|견뎌야 한다. 반드시 버텨야 한다.
 22|
 23|오직 그 일념(一念)으로 이를 악물었다. 시야를 물들인 휘황한 빛줄기 사이로, 쉴 새 없이 뒤집히는 땅과 하늘이 스쳐 지나갔다.
 24|
 25|드넓은 황야. 초승달처럼 굽이진 언덕으로 이어진 사막.
 26|
 27|수백 킬로미터가 넘는 거리가 순식간에 지워지고, 거칠게 요동치던 섬광이 빠르게 사그라졌다.
 28|
 29|그리고 마침내 짙은 어둠이 내려앉았을 때.
 30|
 31|화아악.
 32|
 33|공간이 갈라졌다. 그 틈새 너머로 조금 전의 섬광과는 다른 새로운 빛이 스며들었다.
 34|
 35|아니, 새로운 것은 비단 그뿐만이 아니다.
 36|
 37|‘이건…….’
 38|
 39|보인다. 느껴진다.
 40|
 41|어둡지도, 밝지도 않은 어스름한 빛과 축축한 새벽 공기.
 42|
 43|바람에 섞인 모래알, 거기에 더해 마력(魔力)만이 지닌 특유의 끈적하고 불쾌한 감각까지.
 44|
 45|‘됐다.’
 46|
 47|나는 직감했다.
 48|
 49|이 위험천만한 시도가 성공했다는 것을.
 50|
 51|대마도사가 발휘한 텔레포트 마법이 마력의 방해를 뚫고 정해진 좌표로 우리를 인도했다는 것을.
 52|
 53|그리고 마침내 도달한 그 낯선 공간 너머에, 그토록 찾아 헤매던 한 존재가 있었다.
 54|
 55|도플갱어(Doppelganger).
 56|
 57|“……!”
 58|
 59|허공에서 맞닥트린 시선. 동시에 커지는 눈동자.
 60|
 61|나는 도플갱어를, 도플갱어는 나를 바라보았다.
 62|
 63|마치 세상이 멈춘 것처럼 시간이 느릿하게 흘렀다.
 64|
 65|그러나 이미 해야 할 일을 알고 있는 몸은 시간과 공간을 거스르며 나아갔다.
 66|
 67|슈확.
 68|
 69|창날을 타고 좌우로 갈라진 바람이 귓가를 스친다.
 70|
 71|손아귀에 틀어쥔 백염(白炎)의 창대를 뒤로 젖히자, 뼈가 어긋나는 소리와 함께 예상치 못했던 통증이 밀려들었다.
 72|
 73|우두둑.
 74|
 75|불안정했던 텔레포트 마법의 후유증이다.
 76|
 77|고작 수백 미터를 이동했던 도플갱어의 블링크 마법과는 달리, 수백 킬로미터를 뛰어넘은 위험한 시도의 대가는 고스란히 몸뚱어리가 치러야 했다.
 78|
 79|‘빌어먹을.’
 80|
 81|호흡이 끊기고 손끝이 흔들린다. 창날 위로 내달리던 열양지기가 몸의 이상을 눈치채고 주춤거리는 것이 느껴졌다.
 82|
 83|하지만 그 모든 것은 기우(杞憂)에 불과했다.
 84|
 85|지금의 나는 혼자가 아니었으니까.
 86|
 87|툭.
 88|
 89|강한 힘이 실린 단단한 손이 등을 짚었다. 스켈레톤 킹의 또렷한 음성이 귓가를 파고들었다.
 90|
 91|- 가라.
 92|
 93|그 순간.
 94|
 95|후웅!
 96|
 97|나는 쏘아졌다.
 98|
 99|텔레포트 마법이 벌린 공간의 틈새를 찢고, 벼락처럼 내리꽂혔다. 잠시 주춤하던 열양지기가 들불처럼 일어나 창날을 휘감았다.
100|
101|화륵.
102|
103|뜨거운 열기가 퍼져 나간다. 십여 미터의 공간이 단숨에 지워진다.
104|
105|그리고 그 끝에, 이 예상치 못한 상황 앞에서 눈을 부릅뜬 채 선 도플갱어가 있었다.
106|
107|“이……!”
108|
109|무슨 말을 하려 했을까. 무슨 말이 그토록 하고 싶었을까.
110|
111|하지만 그 누구도, 심지어 놈조차도 그 뒷말을 들을 수 없었다.
112|
113|아니, 이을 수 없었다.
114|
115|콰아아아!
116|
117|파도처럼 터져 나온 청백색의 화염이, 채 끝맺지 못한 외침과 함께 도플갱어의 몸뚱어리를 집어삼켰다.
118|
119|
120|
121|* * *
122|
123|
124|
125|도플갱어는 몸부림쳤다.
126|
127|그것은 지금껏 겪었던 무수한 죽음 중에서도 손꼽힐 만큼 끔찍한 고통이었고, 진정한 의미의 화마(火魔)였다.
128|
129|서걱. 화아악.
130|
131|상반신을 비스듬히 가르고 지나간 창날과 함께, 용암 같은 기운이 도플갱어의 전신 곳곳으로 스며들어 몸부림쳤다.
132|
133|죽음과 동시에 빈 자리를 차지한 생명력을 계속해서 갉아먹으며.
134|
135|피를 증발시키고, 살과 뼈를 녹이며.
136|
137|“크아아아악!”
138|
139|도플갱어는 고통에 찬 비명을 토해 냈다.
140|
141|몸 안으로 침투한 화염은 이미 십여 개의 목숨을 잿더미로 만들었다. 끊임없이 회복되는 살과 뼈가 소방관 역할을 해 주지 않았다면, 지금 이 순간조차도 죽어 가고 있었을 것이다.
142|
143|“끄으으.”
144|
145|실핏줄이 터져 나가 붉게 물든 눈동자.
146|
147|도플갱어가 고통 어린 신음과 함께 허리를 편 그 순간.
148|
149|쐐액, 푹!
150|
151|비틀거리던 몸을 가누기도 전에 날아든 무언가가 미간을 관통한다.
152|
153|뒤로 기울어지던 신형이 지면에 닿기도 전에 부활한 도플갱어가 황급히 옆으로 몸을 날렸다.
154|
155|푸푸푸푹!
156|
157|아슬아슬하게 몸뚱어리를 스치며 지면에 틀어박히는 새하얀 무언가.
158|
159|그것들의 정체가 뼛조각이라는 것을 파악한 도플갱어가 고개를 들었다.
160|
161|더없이 익숙하면서도, 한편으로는 이질적인 기운을 지닌 존재가 그를 향해 쇄도하고 있었다.
162|
163|‘저놈은……!’
164|
165|스켈레톤 킹.
166|
167|한낱 언데드 몬스터에게는 과분한, 그러나 결코 무시할 수 없는 기운이 실린 검신이 번뜩였다.
168|
169|서걱!
170|
171|예리한 절삭음.
172|
173|[영웅의 검]이라는 이름과는 전혀 어울리지 않는, 휘황한 빛을 흩뿌리는 마력이 손목을 가른다.
174|
175|격통과 함께 물러난 도플갱어가 사나운 목소리로 부르짖었다.
176|
177|“감히 언데드 따위가……!”
178|
179|무수한 몬스터가 존재하는 마계(魔界)에서도 언데드의 위치는 맨 밑바닥.
180|
181|이미 지고한 영역에 오른 뒤에야 스스로 언데드가 되기를 선택한 리치(Lich) 같은 존재가 아니라면, 언데드는 한낱 병졸에 불과했다.
182|
183|아니, 분명 그럴 터였다.
184|
185|퍼걱, 촤아아악!
186|
187|눈부신 검광과 함께 터져 나오는 핏물.
188|
189|순식간에 또 한 번의 죽음을 맞이한 도플갱어가 이를 악물었다.
190|
191|‘빌어먹을.’
192|
193|짧은 공방이었지만 내심 인정할 수밖에 없었다. 스켈레톤 킹은 결코 쉬운 상대가 아니라는 것을.
194|
195|눈앞의 저 변종이, 평범한 언데드의 한계를 깨트리고 높은 격에 다다른 존재라는 것을.
196|
197|하지만…….
198|
199|‘저 괴물만큼은 아니지.’
200|
201|스켈레톤 킹을 피해 훌쩍 물러난 도플갱어의 시선이 빠르게 움직였다.
202|
203|깊숙이 가라앉은 그의 눈동자에, 한 자루의 창을 지팡이 삼아 거칠게 호흡을 몰아쉬는 진태경의 모습이 비쳤다.
204|
205|‘마지막으로 봤던 것과는 다르다. 놈도 한계 이상의 힘을 사용한 것이 분명해.’
206|
207|도플갱어는 우둔하지 않다.
208|
209|아니, 여느 인간이나 몬스터와 비교해도 월등하게 교활했다.
210|
211|지난 수십여 년간 미카엘 실베르트라는 허수아비의 뒤에 숨어 세상을 주무를 만큼.
212|
213|그리고 조금 전 갑작스럽게 나타난 진태경의 일격 앞에서도, 지크프리트 바스만의 영혼을 다른 것으로 바꿔치기할 만큼.
214|
215|‘깃들어라.’
216|
217|콰아아.
218|
219|도플갱어를 중심으로 휘몰아치는 강렬한 바람. 심상치 않은 기세를 느낀 스켈레톤 킹이 지면을 박차며 손을 뻗었다.
220|
221|슈확!
222|
223|팔의 뼈 일부가 날카로운 파공성과 함께 공간을 갈랐다. 마치 암기처럼 날아든 새하얀 뼛조각들이 도플갱어의 전신에 틀어박혔다.
224|
225|아니, 스켈레톤 킹의 눈에는 그렇게 보였다.
226|
227|피를 흩뿌리며 쓰러져야 했을 도플갱어의 신형이, 마치 처음부터 그 자리에 없었던 것처럼 지워지기 전까지는.
228|
229|팟.
230|
231|사라졌다. 말 그대로 눈 깜빡할 사이에.
232|
233|그리고 그것은 한 가지 사실을 의미했다.
234|
235|마법.
236|
237|‘블링크(Blink)?’
238|
239|스켈레톤 킹은 불현듯 찾아온 깨달음과 동시에 본능적으로 몸을 비틀었다.
240|
241|그러나 찰나의 순간 허를 찔러 시야를 벗어난 도플갱어는, 이미 그다음을 준비하고 있었다.
242|
243|그그그극.
244|
245|느려진 세상 속에서 마나가 격동한다.
246|
247|그 중심에는 생전 위대했던 대마도사의 모든 것을 탐욕스럽게 집어삼키고, 흡수하여 자신의 배를 불린 몬스터가 있었다.
248|
249|‘에어 슬래시(Air Slash).’
250|
251|그 순간.
252|
253|슈화아아악!
254|
255|스켈레톤 킹을 향해 빗발치는 바람의 칼날을 바라보며, 도플갱어는 확신했다.
256|
257|저것이 당장 저 변종을 소멸시키지는 못하더라도, 잠시나마 전투 불능 상태로 빠트릴 수 있을 만큼 위력적인 마법이라고.
258|
259|이 지긋지긋한 싸움을 끝낼 수 있으리라고.
260|
261|하지만 착각이었다.
262|
263|스켈레톤 킹이 순간적으로 도플갱어를 시야에서 놓쳤듯이, 도플갱어 역시 한 사람의 존재를 망각하고 있었으니.
264|
265|화륵.
266|
267|십여 미터 위 허공에 떠올라 있던 도플갱어는, 문득 자신을 향해 솟구치는 열기를 느꼈다.
268|
269|그제야 조금 전까지만 하더라도 제 몸조차 제대로 가누지 못하고 있던 누군가가 떠올랐다.
270|
271|‘이런 미친……!’
272|
273|헛숨을 삼킨 도플갱어가 황급히 마나를 되돌린 순간.
274|
275|후욱.
276|
277|스켈레톤 킹을 집어삼킬 듯이 떨어져 내리던 광풍(狂風)이 산들바람이 되어 흩어졌다. 동시에 반투명한 방어막이 도플갱어의 전신을 겹겹이 뒤덮었다.
278|
279|그리고 공간을 가로질러 날아든 눈부신 섬광이, 마침내 방어막의 표면과 맞닿은 그때.
280|
281|콰직!
282|
283|도플갱어는 똑똑히 들을 수 있었다. 볼 수 있었다.
284|
285|수십 겹의 실드 마법을 파고드는 한 줄기의 불꽃과, 산산이 부서지는 마나의 방패를.
286|
287|꽈아아앙!
288|
289|발화. 분쇄. 폭발.
290|
291|세 가지 일이 동시에 일어났고, 허공을 물들인 청백색의 화염과 함께 거대한 충격파가 사방을 후려쳤다.
292|
293|구구구구궁!
294|
295|지면까지 고스란히 전해지는 충격을 느낀 스켈레톤 킹은 찰나의 순간 생각했다.
296|
297|어쩌면 지금의 일격으로, 도플갱어는 가장 귀중한 영혼 중 하나를 잃었을지도 모르겠다고.
298|
299|그러나 진태경은 아니었다.
300|
301|힘든 와중에도 젖 먹던 힘까지 끌어 올려 일격을 날린 그는 누구보다 정확하게 알고 있었다.
302|
303|이제는 익숙해져 버린 맑은 종소리가, 왜 지금만큼은 들리지 않는지.
304|
305|‘아직, 아직이다.’
306|
307|놈은, 도플갱어는 아직 대마도사의 힘과 영혼을 지니고 있다.
308|

[P101]

*Take hold.*

*KWA-AAH.*

*Whoosh!*

[P110]
*Pop.*

Magic.

*Blink?*

*Grrrrk.*

*Fwoosh.*

[P132]
*Whoosh.*

*KWA-BOOM!*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

[P95]
But…

[P96]
*Not as high as that monster.*

[P97]
The Doppelganger leapt back from the Skeleton King, its gaze shifting quickly.

[P98]
Its sunken eyes found Jin Taekyung breathing hard, leaning on his spear like a cane.

[P99]
*He’s different from the last time I saw him. He must have pushed himself beyond his limits, too.*

[P100]
The Doppelganger was no fool.

[P101]
It was far more cunning than most humans or monsters. It had manipulated the world for decades from behind its puppet, Michael Silbert.

[P102]
And when Jin Taekyung had appeared without warning and struck, it had swapped Siegfried Bassman’s soul for another.

[P103]
*Take hold.*

[P104]
*KWA-AAH.*

[P105]
A fierce wind whipped around the Doppelganger. Sensing the ominous aura, the Skeleton King kicked off the ground and thrust out his hand.

[P106]
*Whoosh!*

[P107]
Pieces of his arm bone cut through the air with a sharp whistle. The white fragments flew like hidden weapons and lodged throughout the Doppelganger’s body.

[P108]
Or so the Skeleton King thought.

[P109]
The figure that should have fallen in a spray of blood vanished as though it had never been there.

[P110]
*Pop.*

[P111]
Gone. In the blink of an eye.

[P112]
That meant one thing.

[P113]
Magic.

[P114]
*Blink?*

[P115]
Realization struck, and the Skeleton King twisted instinctively.

[P116]
But the Doppelganger had already slipped from his sight and prepared its next move.

[P117]
*Grrrrk.*

[P118]
Mana surged through the slowing world.

[P119]
At its center was the monster that had greedily swallowed everything the Grand Mage had possessed in life, absorbing it all for itself.

[P120]
*Air Slash.*

[P121]
And then—

[P122]
*Whoooosh!*

[P123]
Blades of wind rained down on the Skeleton King. Watching them, the Doppelganger was certain that even if the spell could not erase the aberration outright, it would put him out of the fight for a while.

[P124]
That would be enough to end this wretched battle.

[P125]
But it was wrong.

[P126]
Just as the Skeleton King had lost sight of the Doppelganger for an instant, the Doppelganger had forgotten someone else.

[P127]
*Fwoosh.*

[P128]
Floating more than ten meters above the ground, it suddenly felt heat rising toward it.

[P129]
Only then did it remember the man who, moments earlier, could barely keep his own body upright.

[P130]
*You’ve got to be fucking kidding me…!*

[P131]
The Doppelganger sucked in a startled breath and hurriedly drew back its mana.

[P132]
*Whoosh.*

[P133]
The gale descending on the Skeleton King dissolved into a gentle breeze. At the same time, layer upon layer of translucent barriers covered the Doppelganger’s body.

[P134]
A dazzling flash shot through the air and struck them.

[P135]
*Crack!*

[P136]
The Doppelganger heard it. Saw it.

[P137]
A single streak of flame bored through dozens of layers of Shield magic, shattering the barriers of mana.

[P138]
*KWA-BOOM!*

[P139]
Ignition. Shattering. Explosion.

[P140]
All three happened at once. Blue-white flames filled the air, and a massive shock wave lashed out in every direction.

[P141]
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*

[P142]
The Skeleton King felt the impact reach the ground. For an instant, he wondered if that strike had cost the Doppelganger one of its most precious souls.

[P143]
Jin Taekyung knew better.

[P144]
Exhausted as he was, he had scraped together every last bit of strength for that strike. He knew better than anyone why the clear, familiar chime had not sounded.

[P145]
*Not yet. Not yet.*

[P146]
The bastard still had the Grand Mage’s power and soul.

[P147]
But his legs, which should already have driven him off the ground, would not move.

[P148]
His depleted mental strength kept dragging his consciousness toward a bottomless pit. The dozens of movements and attack routes flashing through his mind were no more than things he could imagine doing.

[P149]
All he had was a friend who could read his intent from a glance.

[P150]
*Bang!*

[P151]
Their eyes met for an instant across the open air.

[P152]
That was enough. The Skeleton King read the look in Jin Taekyung’s eyes and launched himself off the ground without hesitation.

[P153]
Through the acrid smoke filling the air.

[P154]
Toward the Doppelganger at the center of the explosion.

[P155]
*Tssssss!*

[P156]
Golden magical power surged along his blade.

[P157]
The strain of the reckless Teleport had left him with less than half his usual strength, but the dazzling sword light cut through the sky without slowing.

[P158]
It sliced through the thick smoke and shot toward the enemy beyond.

[P159]
*Shing!*

[P160]
A single streak of light.

[P161]
At the end of that keen strike—

[P162]
*Shhk!*

[P163]
Crimson blood burst forth like a fountain.

[P164]
* * *

[P165]
My vision was slowly blurring, but I saw it clearly.

[P166]
The Skeleton King’s strike cutting through the air. An arm rising through the spray of blood.

[P167]
*He cut it off.*

[P168]
No doubt about it. That slender white arm belonged to the Doppelganger—or, more precisely, to the Grand Mage it had absorbed three years ago.

[P169]
But no head fell. No scream came.

[P170]
If I hadn’t spotted where the Doppelganger had gone after vanishing from sight again, I might have shouted in frustration.

[P171]
Instead, I swallowed my anger.

[P172]
My voice came out exhausted and unfamiliar, as though it belonged to someone else.

[P173]
“Are you a fucking lizard or something, you son of a bitch?”

[P174]
I turned slowly. The Doppelganger stood in the middle of the ruins, blood pouring from its cleanly severed shoulder.

[P175]
“Let’s go for your head this time. Not an arm or a leg—your head. How’s that?”

[P176]
“I’m afraid that won’t be possible.”

[P177]
Its face twisted like a Fiend’s, the Doppelganger continued.

[P178]
“I’ll need the Grand Mage’s soul for what comes next.”

[P179]
*What?*

[P180]
I was about to ask when—

[P181]
*Vwoom.*

[P182]
An immense power pulsed around it.

[P183]
No. The entire ruin trembled like a living creature.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
